brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: piano + color wheel + chord names creates a memorable, playful synesthetic interaction model
Vivid HSL gradient wheel anchors the composition with high visceral pull and clear harmony-point indicators
Palette swatches read cleanly with mono hex labels, giving immediate scannability of generated chord-colors
dominant_weaknesses: Three-panel layout feels disconnected — piano floats at bottom, right rail is a plain form, wheel dominates without visual bridges
Typography is generic system stack with weak hierarchy; 'Chromatic Harmonizer' gradient title clashes tonally with the utilitarian sidebars
Chord buttons (D Major, F# Minor, A Major) sit awkwardly beside the keyboard with no grouping container or alignment logic
fix_priorities: Unify piano + chord chips into one instrument module with shared container and tighter spatial relationship to wheel
Replace generic UI typography with a more expressive display face for chord/note names to honor the musical metaphor
Strengthen visual coupling between played notes and wheel positions via animated arcs or shared color glow
Tighten right rail — collapse redundant color format fields and elevate Export as a distinct action zone
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral leads via the saturated wheel and playful piano, reflective concept is strong, but behavioral clarity lags because the cause-effect between keys, chords, and wheel points isn't visually wired.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the piano-as-palette-instrument metaphor is executed literally and legibly, though the harmony 'locking' moment needs more kinetic feedback to truly feel like chords snapping into place.
